author: reek
body: A combo device -- boot keyboard on one interface, boot mouse on the next, the wireless-dongle shape -- under the per-interface walk. The whole-device classifier this replaces handed the entire device to the keyboard driver and the mouse half was unreachable, which is why no pointer had ever moved over USB in any bed.

author: reek
body: `-hid-combo` gives codex-vm's root HID device both interfaces; `-hid-keys` routes the scripted keys through USB alone; the `-mouse` timeline moves the pointer to (60,40) and presses the left button. `same-dev=1` proves both handles sit on ONE slot, `got=30` that the keyboard half still types with SET_CONFIGURATION sent exactly once, and `pos=60,40 btn=1` that boot mouse reports travel their own interrupt pipe into the folded position.

author: reek
body: The wait is bounded by the RTC rather than by an iteration count: each pump costs several VM exits, so a count large enough to cover the timeline in iterations is minutes of wall clock.
